title: Lekalo Target Protocol
description: Closed wire contract for the lekalo.target/v1 process protocol that connects the Lekalo core to external target adapters running as separate executables in any language; one request on stdin or a bounded temporary file, one response envelope on stdout, diagnostics and logs on stderr only, with version and capability negotiation over the describe handshake, deterministic request identifiers, declared output plans verified against observed writes, and the infrastructure/protocol/operation error classification. Version 0.3.1 additively extended the describe response capabilities with declared IR contract versions, named capability support states, and optional declared constraints; extended scan entries with the closed typed evidence member; and extended request envelopes with the resolved profile digest and capability snapshot. Version 0.3.2 adds one read-only operation plan-native: its request alone carries the required native_request member (bounded changed files/symbols, scan evidence and input custody, observed and execution-policy references, tool catalog and capability snapshot digests), and its successful result alone carries the required native_plan member — the proposed immutable native gate plan the adapter planner proposes without reading or executing anything; the member is forbidden on every other operation, dry_run, plan_id and writes stay forbidden on plan-native, and the frozen 0.3.1 documents keep their exact published meanings. Successor 0.6.4 adds lint, lint_request and lint_evidence. This read-only static collector never executes application code or native gates. Issue #95: explicitly declared read-only watch selection partitions. Full captured IR is resolution context only; module work validates/scans only the named partition (including removed symbols), global work only mandatory cross-module obligations. Every selected response echoes the SHA-256 of the canonical selection bytes. Legacy calls have no selection or echo. Successor 0.9.0 retains the 0.8.0 wire surface and admits scan entry detail up to 2048 Unicode code points, so complete semantic/native/test binding evidence fits without truncation. Other operations retain the 128-character bound. Successful scans require exact source and normalized launch-profile digests. Watch selection still requires an explicit adapter capability declaration. Successor 0.9.1 carries the complete immutable native plan in successful plan-native responses. Its digest and bounded summary must agree with the complete document; a summary alone cannot authorize production execution. Every predecessor keeps its published wire members. Successor 1.1.0 carries a complete bounded native declaration subtree per scan entry, preserving lexical ownership, exact names, source positions and structural digests. Root/cycle/owner/span consistency is additionally validated by the runtime. Old contracts retain their original members and refusals.

depends_on.description: The selected commands that must run first (command ids, issue #61 successor semantics).

NativePlan_workspaceRoot.description: The workspace root: the explicit special case '.' for standalone/root packages, or one canonical logical path. Never a wildcard grant.

NativePlanDocument.title: Lekalo Native Gate Execution Plan
NativePlanDocument.description: Closed contract for one immutable native gate execution plan Successor of the v0.3.2 native gate plan (issue #61; the v0.3.2 enums are never silently broadened). Closed contract for one immutable native gate execution plan (issue #48): the discovered workspace and package graph, the input and scan custody digests, the changed inputs, the affected-package closure with per-package reasons and exclusions, the proposed gate commands with exact relative cwd, literal argv, env recipe, tool references, dependencies and per-command limits, the capability snapshot, the whole-run run eligibility, and the plan digest over the canonical plan with the digest member absent. The plan is a proposal only: it never authorizes its own execution — an external approval naming this exact digest is required, and the approval never lives inside the plan.
